Then you were asked whether there were more local Serbs or soldiers, and you said that there were a bit more local Serbs. Do you remember stating that? I read this from the transcript from page 652.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you about the conversation with the officer, because on page 656 it says that you spoke for that officer for as long as an hour, and today you clarified that and said that your whole stay there was much shorter, and you spoke during that time to soldiers and the officer and so on, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: However, looking at that transcript I was unable to see that you described seeing anything taking place in the hangar or anybody being taken out of the hangar. Do you remember whether this was because no such questions were put to you or is there any other reason?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered the questions that were put to me. I answered whatever they asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It seems to me that you did not speak of this today and yesterday. Dodaj Hajdar, Kuscevic and Hrkic were with you, both in Negoslavci and in Topcider. However, they were not in the indictment nor were they tried and, in fact, if I'm right, the two of them were proposed as witnesses in the trial against you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is it true that you stated that the two of them, I'm now referring to Kuscevic and Hrkic, testified about you and Dodaj committing some crimes, and that -- that's what I spoke about?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During our stay in Topcider we wrote dozens of statements. The two of them, under duress, wrote a statement because they were pressured into it. For example, to write that several soldiers were killed by them and so on. They said that they didn't do it. But then they were beaten and they were pressured, and they were asked, "Well, if you didn't do it, who did." And then in order to get themselves out, they blamed us for it. So they told these untruths about us in order to ease their own position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is this your assumption, or do you have something to corroborate this? How do you know that they stressed -- said this under duress? Is it only on the basis of knowing that this was not true?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they would come to see what Dodaj and I were writing, and then they would say, "You didn't write anything bad about your friends, they wrote such things about you, so why don't you write about them, why don't you write that they did this and that." And I told them that I was unable to write that because as far as I knew, they did nothing wrong, just like I didn't, and I couldn't write anything that wasn't true, and I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So based on that you concluded that they wrote something that wasn't true, and they did it under duress and shifted the blame on you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And I suppose that you were unable to contact them at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody could contact anyone or talk to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Upon your return to Croatia and later, did you have any health problems, were you treated for any condition? If necessary, we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What type of problems did you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we should go into private session after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I have no further questions for you, except -- although this may not be necessary either, but let me say to you that the position of the Defence of Mr. Mrksic is that he was never at Ovcara, not even on the occasion when you were there. However, we were able to clarify this with you by checking whether you were sure that you saw such a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I would like to ask the usher to give to the witness the statement he gave to the Prosecution, because I intend to use it. Thank you. Witness, you have before you the statement given to the OTP if I need to remind you of something you stated at the time. My first question to you is: You had military training before you came to the Vukovar front, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The training lasted for several months. The answer was not recorded. And your answer was what? When I said that you had several months worth of training.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a fast-track training, an abbreviated one, and it may have lasted three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During that training you were taught about the JNA uniforms, branches of service, ranks and so on, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you please turn to the page 3, paragraph 5, that's in English version, and you have the page in front of you. When describing the arrival of soldiers on the 19th of November to the hospital, you described in detail who approached you, what you talked about. That was a brief conversation though. Then you described the situation with Zoran and so on, and so on. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: However, when asked by my learned friend you said that this was a soldier. In the statement given to the OTP, the statement in front of you, do you see that in relation to all of these three elements you said three times: "One of the soldiers, a military policeman approached me." And then: "Serbian policeman recognised Zoran." And then you said: "After some time military policemen came and picked up." Would you please look at your statement and confirm that this is in the text, that you mentioned the word "military policemen" three times in relation to these elements that I just quoted to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you stand by your previous statement that this was a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you now describe for us the uniform of that military policeman? Can you describe his uniform, what he had on his head, whether he had some belts?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did. He had a uniform, naturally, had a helmet on his head. Had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how did you know that he was a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he had a white belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Following that you described the event which took place on the 20th in the morning in the hospital. And on page 3, paragraph 7 of the English version you said this: "In the morning the hospital staff told us to move towards the exit." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that they were the only ones who gave you that order at that time in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hospital staff told us, and we knew that an evacuation of the hospital had been agreed, and that the hospital staff, together with Mrs. Bosanac, went to discuss this with Mr. Mrksic, and that everything had been arranged.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you well, this order and this recommendation was given solely by the hospital staff, namely that you were to go out in front of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, and I'm not sure whether you mentioned this yesterday in your testimony, but in your statement, page 3, paragraph 7 of the English version, and the page is in front of you, you stated as follows: "I saw buses parked on the road. Members of the military police ordered us to stand in one line, put our hands behind our backs and keep our heads lowered." Is that in your statement? Would you please look at it? The other highlighted portion.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question on this is: What were these military policemen wearing on the 20th of November in the morning in front of the hospital when this was happening?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not just the military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: First I'm asking you about the military policemen and then we will continue. How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are going too fast.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing uniforms, cross belts, helmets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did any of their superior officers there issue orders how they should search you, how you should go to the bus, did they have a superior officer there, these military policemen?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only one that I was able to see who was there was -- I don't know exactly what he was, that's Captain Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You explained that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in charge, nobody else was issuing orders, nor could have been issuing orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean you didn't see any officers ordering the military policemen to search you and to send you to the buses other than what you have just said now?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I saw was Sljivancanin and that he was in charge and that everything went through him, that he was the person in charge there and that he was organising everything in agreement with the rest of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But did you see him issue direct orders? You assume that he was in charge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him going in and out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What were the officers that you saw there wearing? This is also stated in your statement. You also said yourself that there were other officers there, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What were they wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, can you please describe that.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, if the officers were wearing camouflage uniforms, caps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What kind of caps?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The camouflage caps with the flags, blue, white and red.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see -- well, what was the visibility like at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was when we left the hospital, between 8.00 and 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was it visible? Could you see well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course you could.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you sure that you saw all of this well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And nobody was dressed differently? I'm speaking about the officers. They were not dressed differently than the way you described?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You also said in your statement to the OTP on page 3, paragraph 7 of the English version, that the officers searched you, that they were there. So you confirmed actually what you just said now?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please turn to the next page? For my learned friends from the Prosecution, this is page 4, paragraph 4. I'm going to read it for you to make it easier for you. "After a short drive we reached the Vukovar barracks." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: It also says here: "Members of the military police then took those people away." You said that and we talked about that today. And now this last sentence is the most important: "I did not see there any of the JNA officers who were in front of the hospital." Is this correct, that you said this? So all the officers that you registered in front of the entrance to the hospital or the exit to the hospital, you did not see any of them at the barracks during the time you were there until you left for Ovcara; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with this, I would like to complete my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day once again, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, good day. I am Novak Lukic, and I am one of the Defence team of Mr. Sljivancanin, and I'm going to be putting some questions to you. I don't want to go into questions that you've already replied to. I'm going to make brief pauses just to make sure I don't ask the same questions again. I would just like to put a couple of questions in regard to the detailed answers you gave to Mr. Domazet concerning your proceedings before the military court. Can we now please look at a document on the monitor? This is the judgement against you which we received from the Prosecution. In e-court it's 2D04-0008. You will see it in front of you on the screen, this document. Can we just zoom in on the document a little bit more, please. And could we look at the middle part of the judgement. Thank you very much. If we can scroll down. Thank you very much. Very briefly, Mr. Zlogledja, do you -- are you familiar with this document, this judgement by the -- the verdict by the military court in Belgrade of the 2nd of March, 1992? It has a number of pages.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I, and we will not be dealing with the details here, but factually what we described, or in your defence before that tribunal you described the things identically in the way you described them in front of this Tribunal --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel is too fast, we cannot interpret all of his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the tribunal your testimony coincides with the testimony you provided here in relation to the facts that you talked about here.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a certain extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please introduce this exhibit into the file.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 559, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You already testified today that you had contacts with Mr. Dodaj practically here when you testified in 1998 because you were in The Hague at the same time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that you spent time together, then I assume you did not discuss the case or the testimony then?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a lady here who said that we should not be discussing those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Are you aware that he testified before you in this case here that is underway right now? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, in this trial on the Vukovar three accused.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that he testified here in The Hague before I did in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you given the status of a defender of Vukovar, and did you receive all the benefits arising from that status in accordance with the regulations of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps receive a rank or some kind of recognition?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During all these years, did you ever go back to visit Vukovar during the anniversaries of certain events there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went to Vukovar since.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You already talked about how you decided to join the defenders of Vukovar. I'm not going to go into those details --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- although I did prepare some questions on that. I'm just going to ask you about one detail. Do you remember any episodes during your, let's say, fighting in Vukovar when Petar Kuscevic brought two tanks from the Trpinjska Cesta road? Do you remember anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do remember him doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how this came about, how did he manage to bring in two tanks from the other side, from the JNA? Do you know any details about that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think that there was some fighting there, there was a clash, the tanks stayed behind, and that he brought back those two tanks. I wasn't there. That's it, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether those tanks were then later used by your units?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that tank or two tanks only had a couple of shells. So there were no shells left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I'm going to move to, let's say, your decision to go to the hospital. Yesterday and today you explained some details about that. And yesterday you testified that when you took Lorenc, and today we hear that after that you changed and then you came to the hospital. But you said yesterday that according to you that was the safest place, the hospital.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is: When you came to the hospital and when you decided to stay, did you ask anyone there if you were permitted to stay at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask anyone. This was just towards the end, and all the civilians, the elderly, women, children, were pouring into the hospital seeking shelter. And they kept coming in larger groups. They were much safer and felt that they would be more likely to survive there than if they remained in some basement or cellar somewhere. They were afraid that they would be liquidated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understand that, that's what part of what you said yesterday. But you did not answer my question. Did you ask anyone if were you permitted to stay at the hospital, this is my question, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did ask personnel, the personnel there, the staff there. I think that it was mainly the director, but I did ask some of the personnel there. Nobody told us to leave, nobody threw us out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the point in time when you decided to stay, and as you say when you asked any of the staff, you were not sick, you were not wounded and no family members were amongst the personnel or the wounded at the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During those couple of days that you stayed at the hospital before the evacuation, other than the people you already mentioned, did you see anyone else from the police station, or of the defenders whom you knew from before, from combat operations or during the defence of Vukovar that came there in the same way that you did? Do you remember anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a young man, the same age as me, perhaps he was a couple of years older than me, I do remember him, he was an active policeman in the Croatian police. He was also at the hospital. But he left when the evacuation was carried out the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're thinking of the 19th, most probably when all the civilians were transferred in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the civilians left, only the wounded stayed at the hospital. Perhaps there were a few more who tried to stay behind, but I know that he left in that evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard testimony before this Tribunal that some defenders in the last days and nights bandaged healthy parts of their body, they bandaged themselves and put on patients' gowns. Did you see or hear anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anyone doing that, but I also heard myself that there were such attempts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of the surrender of the Mitnica group headed by Filip Karaula in those days? We know specifically that it was on the 17th of November, but did you hear about that when you were in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall hearing anything about that. I know that that was done, but I don't know who surrendered when and where. That is something that I really couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP, and I will provide the statements for you to look at, you said that in the room when you were in the hospital you were together with Dodaj in the -- on the ground floor of the hospital. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the basement of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you were together with Dodaj then?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dodaj was there. They were coming to this room, and they were moving around the hospital too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have just -- we have just heard about that, but you didn't testify about that. Perhaps you testified about that in the Dokmanovic case, but you didn't state that before this Trial Chamber. Do you agree that on the 19th, in the afternoon, the transfer of all civilians from the hospital was organised, and we know that this was in the direction of Velepromet. Do you know anything about that, and did you personally then decide to remain at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I know that there were evacuations of civilians, all of them, and I decided at any cost to stay at the hospital, and I stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that was your decision entirely at that time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You described yesterday how some people on the 19th, in the evening, were taken out by local Serbs and reservists, or rather that night. But in the statement to The Hague Tribunal, to the OTP, you said something that I'm going to read to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please provide a copy of the statement for the witness so he can have that in front of him? You have -- do you have the statement in front of you? Could you please look at your statement, take the statement that you gave to the OTP. This is page 3 of the B/C/S version; I think it's also page 3 of the English, one paragraph but last. You are describing the events of the 19th in the hospital, so you said the following. "It seems to me that during the night I heard -- I think I saw members of some international organisations inside the hospital." Are you following me, can you see where we are?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't -- I haven't found the place yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. I have a redacted version. Let me just find it, so we were just ... Yes, I obviously have here now, this is page 4, page 4. This is the top paragraph. Actually, the second paragraph from the top, I am reading line 2. It begins: "I heard from the hospital staff." Have you found that paragraph? It's page 4: "I heard from the hospital staff that we all should leave the hospital." Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just a moment. Paragraph 2. I think it's not quite properly translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are many things like that. But anyway, the second sentence states: "I think that during the night I saw members of some international organisation inside the hospital. I think I remember them wearing white uniforms and some kind of blue marks on their sleeves, but that is about all I remember." Do you remember stating this to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most probably that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you just remember seeing them, but you don't recall the details. I'm going to ask you, do you remember if they were recording down some names, did they speak with anyone from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we now put Exhibit 338 on the screen, please, which is a photograph marked with 0036-6975. The other photograph. The other photograph I marked in the set, 0036-6975. Thank you. I will ask you whether the persons you remember seeing on the 19th in the evening looked roughly like the people on these photographs in terms of their clothing, that they had something white on their sleeves?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seemed to me then that I saw them. But it only seemed to me, so I wasn't sure 100 per cent. Perhaps it was more me wishing to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. But if that's how it was, if there is a picture vividly in your mind, did these people look similar to these in the picture?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it's time for the break. Or shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see Mrs. Vesna Bosanac while you were in the hospital for a couple of days?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see her previously in the police station coming there while you were there? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that. And I never saw her in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you saw her for the first time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you know that was her?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew. We were told. I asked who this lady is, and we heard that she was the director, Dr. Vesna Bosanac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you spoke to her?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I spoke to her personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember another detail? When I asked you about people who were taken away on the 19th, did you hear that she said, or did somebody convey that she said that all civilians were to leave the hospital on the 19th? Did you hear anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard, yes, from the hospital staff, and there were a number of them, that the civilians were all to leave the hospital on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Another question having to do with the fact that you spent most of your time in Vukovar at the police station. Did you hear that 140 members of the Varazdin police station were engaged in Vukovar during combat operations there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know how many people and where they were from, but I knew that there was something like that, that there were some policemen from Varazdin, but I didn't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now turn to the events of the 20th of November. I looked carefully at your evidence in the Dokmanovic case where you tried to be very specific about your movements on that day in terms of the time-line. On page 644 of the Dokmanovic transcript you said that you went into the hallway between -- between 8.00. Yesterday you said between 6.00 and 8.00, which is not entirely relevant, but at around that time. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We came out at around 8.00 and left the hospital perhaps at 9.00 or 9.30, and this is when we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. On page 648 of the Dokmanovic transcript you said that you travelled from the hospital to the barracks about half an hour, and that you reached the barracks, in your view, at around 11.00. Is it possible that it was then that you reached the barracks?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you how long we travelled for. All I know is that we left the hospital, we came to the Vukovar barracks, and stopped there. Now, as for the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zlogledja, I'm reading to you your evidence in the Dokmanovic trial, where you testified under oath. You will agree with me that back in 1998 your memory was better than today, 14 years after the events, so that's why I'm asking you whether it was possible.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I most likely stated this, so it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then yesterday you said, as you did on page 649 in the Dokmanovic transcript, that you spent about two hours in the barracks. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then on page 651 you said that travelling from the barracks to the field where the Ovcara hangar is located, you travelled for -- or rather, that that trip took about 20 minutes. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are some discrepancies and I'm trying to clarify that. Yesterday you said that you spent a total of half an hour at Ovcara. That's what you said yesterday on page 70.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement given to the OTP, on page 5, you say -- I'm trying to find the page now. On page 6 of the B/C/S version. First sentence, last paragraph. "We spent about 40 minutes with that officer." That's the statement you gave to the OTP. Today you told us that you spoke to him for some 10 minutes, and in the statement it says that you spent 40 minutes with him. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess that that's how it was translated and recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that you talked for 40 minutes with him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For 40 minutes, what could we have possibly discussed for 40 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that he stood next to you for 40 minutes?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as we got off the bus they were waiting for us there, and the first question was, are you all soldiers, which military post, where from, who was your commanding officer. That was the conversation, brief questions. And then he left. And then in that interval, I guess they called the units and established that we had, indeed, been soldiers there. But then when they saw what our ethnic affiliation was, then they realised that we were not imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you told us about that. But you still continued to claim that you talked to that officer for some 10 minutes, that that was a dialogue, or rather a monologue, and that it didn't take 40 minutes, as you stated earlier to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is the good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zlogledja, I have to go back to inconsistencies in your statement. It is your claim that you stayed about half an hour at Ovcara; that's what you told us yesterday and today. You also said that you talked to that officer for how long?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep insisting that I say exactly how long. It's impossible to say five minutes, three minutes, two minutes, in view of the circumstances and the course of events. It's impossible for me to specify it accurately. I told you roughly five to 10 minutes worth of conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you said today that you thought that with that officer and that vehicle you left for Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the statement given to the OTP for which you said that it was probably mistranslated, it says that you spent 40 minutes talking to him, and you signed it back in 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You testified in the Dokmanovic case also under oath, just like here, on page 656, line 4, the question was as follows, it pertains to the conversation with the officer at Ovcara: "[In English] How long did the conversation with the JNA officer last?" [B/C/S spoken]. "[In English] This was up to maybe one hour, perhaps." [Interpretation] I don't think that this was an interpretation error, because this reflects your words as they were translated live. So in 1998 you said that it was up to one hour, and today we heard it was a couple of minutes. Let's see what's true.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is that we were there. Not just the conversation, but the entire time that we spent there was perhaps half an hour, perhaps an hour. It's hard to say exactly how long it was. But the total amount of time we spent at Ovcara was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. So you think that you spent a total of one hour at Ovcara. Let me ask you this. Can you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That wasn't a fair summary. He doesn't know, he says. Maybe up to an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, I don't want to insist on something you can't remember after all these years. I'm just putting inconsistencies to you in the answers you provided then and today. If you do not remember something or can't answer a question, just please say so. Let me ask you something else about the time-line of events. From the moment you came to Ovcara, do you remember in which bus you were?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you already, it was either the penultimate or the ultimate bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How much time elapsed from the moment you reached Ovcara until you got to this colonel? So how long did it take for your bus to disembark, for you to come out and so on?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, let me round it to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Another question that's very important to me. If you spent up to one hour in total at Ovcara, when did the people stop entering the hangar, or rather how much longer did you stay with that colonel there before they stopped beating people in the gauntlet? If you were in the penultimate bus, that means that there was one bus behind you. Is that right? So how long did that take for people from one bus to go through the gauntlet?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 15 minutes, definitely. Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go back to the events at the hospital and then we'll follow the chronology from there on. I will show you a brief video sequence here, Exhibit 118, you will see it on the screen, and then I'll ask for you to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine. We don't need to go further than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, who did you recognise in this footage?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can easily recognise Captain Sljivancanin in this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We know, and we could see on this tape that it was filmed on the 20th of November in the morning when the evacuation was conducted. Since we know that this video was frequently shown in various documentaries, both on Croatian and Belgrade television, I'll ask you this: Do you know where this dialogue took place, the one shown in this video?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of the conflict between Sljivancanin and the representatives of the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you over the years ever watch any TV programmes about Vukovar events, ever?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever I came upon such topic, I would switch to another channel. I didn't feel like watching, and I never watched a documentary that was wholly about Vukovar and what was happening there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see photographs of Major Sljivancanin in press articles after you were released?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. On the 20th in the morning you left the hospital together with a group of your mates, Dodaj, Kuscevic and so on, and then you were frisked from that corridor, which was the side -- near the side entrance to the hospital. On page 644 of the Dokmanovic transcript, you said that they looked for sharp and solid objects, that you were frisked for that.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that we were frisked and checked, yes. Now, whether they were looking for that, I don't know. The soldiers searched us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they take any money that you might have had, or did they just search you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't take anything from me, they just searched me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you stood there in that line, you saw my client?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He went in and out of the hospital, you testified about that yesterday and today, and also in the Dokmanovic trial. He didn't talk to you then, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what you said to The Hague Office of the Prosecutor. So he never addressed you while you stood there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You stood in a line one next to each other; that's how I understood it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether in that line you were towards the end nearer the hospital door, or nearer the yard?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't nearer the entrance into the compound, no. I was closer to the entrance into the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you said to my colleague Borovic that there were other officers there. Did you see them or there were none there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did you use the plural then? You said you did not see the officers who were at the hospital earlier at the barracks. My learned friend, Mr. Borovic, has already confronted you with that, and I do realise that there were more such officers at the hospital whom you did not see at the barracks later. That's your evidence, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we do agree that you did see a number of different officers at the hospital, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You described Sljivancanin going in and out of the hospital building, just appearing there. How many times did you see him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times. He went in and out of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Several times. How long would he stay within your line of sight? 15 minutes, 20 minutes, 30 minutes?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between five and 15, depending.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember Dodaj Hajdar standing anywhere near you in that line?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly if he was next to me or not. I don't remember his exact position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you were on the same bus, right, because you had left together, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were on the same bus. That much is certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is about that. How did you board the buses? Did you just fill up the seats, or could you choose which bus you boarded?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, one by one, starting with the first bus and then all the way to the last bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you were standing in that line in the hospital corridor before you headed for the buses, did you at this time see any international presence in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This was on page 5658 on the 7th of March this year; that's for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. That was the evidence. So you didn't see anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anyone. Not from the time I left the hospital to the time I arrived at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember - if not, please feel free to say so - were you on the left-hand side of the bus or on the right-hand side of the bus and did you have a window seat?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said there were between four and five buses there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yours was second to last, most probably. Were there any other vehicles in that column on its way to the barracks? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the buses, as far as I could tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now about the time-line. You have been asked about this. My conclusion is you spent around two hours at the barracks, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You clearly said that you did not see my client at the barracks, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've heard a lot of evidence here about those buses inside the barracks being parked in a semi-circle on some sort of an elevation?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were all parked within the barracks compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You confirmed what you said yesterday in answer to one of Mr. Domazet's questions, only one person was taken off your bus, a young man from Zagreb. Do you remember at Ovcara being -- questions being asked about some Albanians, but you only remember one person being taken off the bus inside the barracks compound at the time, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was sitting just in front of me, and I know this for a fact. Yes, he was taken off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have heard a lot of evidence about what went on in the barracks, and all of those witnesses who were with you on those buses claim that there was a list, that names were called out, that people were taken off, and that these people would then be beaten on the way from one bus to another. Is this possible, that there was a list, and that names were called out, but you didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be possible. In this specific case, this soldier came up to the window because the young lad was seated next to the window, and said, "That's him. He fired at me." And that's why he was taken off. I'm not sure if anybody else was taken off based on a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're saying only he was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my bus only he was taken off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Dodaj was with you on the bus and Kuscevic was on the bus in front of you, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was a witness who was with you on your bus. This is page 5532, the date is the 6th of March. I'm not mentioning his name. He says that about 10 persons were taken off your bus. Does that strike you as possible?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My bus? No. I don't think as many.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just that one young man, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm positive about that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll remind of something on page 649 -- I can't switch my mic off.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the latter part of counsel's remark.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will now quote from the Dokmanovic case. The page reference is 649. This is the 3rd of February, 1998. Question by the OTP: "[In English] How many with regard to your own bus?" [B/C/S spoken] "From my bus they took out about four men. Four, five men. Five, perhaps." "Q. Do you know their names? "A. I do not know. I think three or four were local people from Vukovar, and there were a boy from Zagreb." 1998. You sound quite determined. You saw four to five people being taken off your bus. Do you remember saying that at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you weren't telling the truth, yesterday or today, or back then? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying all time is I'm sure about that one, and then there were soldiers entering the bus there in front and they may have taken several people off the bus there. Perhaps not 10. I'm only positive about this one who was right in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zlogledja, I'm just telling you what you said yesterday. You said one person. Back in 1998 you seemed quite determined. This is an unequivocal reference to several people from Vukovar being taken off. A question about your observation at the barracks. You say you were told to keep your heads down?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could it be the case that you just couldn't see something because your heads were down most of the time? How would that strike you by way of an inference?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may have been the case. I wasn't really in a position to keep looking at things all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to Ovcara now. You say you left the bus and standing next to this, well practically -- well, let me call him JNA officer, there were Kuscevic and Hrkic standing right next to him, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the Dokmanovic case you described their -- this man's physical appearance and his rank. You said colonel at the time on page 654, didn't you? You described how he questioned you. But the way you testified, and that's why I'm asking, is my conclusion, okay, you say you saw my client then, Sljivancanin. Approaching those people in the gauntlet. My conclusion is the timing when you, as you say, see Sljivancanin, that was in the next 15 minutes before even the last one got into the hangar, right? And the gauntlet was no more. Is my conclusion right? Or if no, please say. What is it? In relation to this period, you're standing there with that colonel, that period of time you were there, when is it that you see Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't come at that time when we were there talking. It wasn't until later on when people had already been taken off the buses and taken inside the hangar. This group of people were standing outside the hangar, those who were beating the people inside, going in and out all the time. It wasn't until later that I saw this captain --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was a major; that has not been challenged.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a major. He talked to those people, and he soon went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Zlogledja, you testified yesterday that you saw him approach those people and talked to them as they were still in the gauntlet beating people. You expected at the time that they would stop the beatings; that's what you said. In the Dokmanovic case, let me jog your memory, sir. That may be in your statement after all, not in the Dokmanovic case. You say that he approached those people who were in the gauntlet beating the people who were running the gauntlet. Let me go back to your statement. It's your statement to the OTP, page 6. "I saw him approach" -- I'm talking about halfway down the page, third passage. "I saw him approach those two lines of soldiers beating the people and I saw him talk to them. He then walked right back to where he came from. He didn't speak to me or anybody else." Based on what you said yesterday, I conclude that you saw Sljivancanin approach those people while those people in the gauntlet, let me say, were near the bus, so how much time would you say elapsed?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. They were all out of the buses and it was only then that he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think there are discrepancies in your testimony, but that's no matter right now. Please tell me this. You were standing -- if you stood there outside the hangar, please tell me now how long before you left for Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a half hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So there is this half-hour period of time. Regardless of which point in time precisely, you see my client, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at one point in time I catch sight of him. That is beyond doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine, let's press on. On page 71 of yesterday's transcript, the draft, you said that Sljivancanin was being accompanied by a driver and that they had arrived there in a Pinzgauer. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that military vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the driver too?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the driver was the one who brought him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP on page 6, you say he was being escorted by other soldiers. This is a plural reference. So was there just a lone driver, or was there a whole group of soldiers tagging along, a group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, the case for both the singular and the plural for this particular noun is the same in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let's see what you said about this in the Dokmanovic case, because there is a different reference there. I see that there is an observation on the transcript. It's because of our language. There is a certain degree of ambiguity in our language. I will now quote the English reference in the OTP's translation, so that we are clear about what I am asking the question about. In your statement you referred to a number of soldiers, not just one. The English reference is 0040-0272. In English you said and signed the statement: "[Previous translation continues] ... [In English] was accompanied by other soldiers." [Interpretation] But fine. Same question, the same question was asked by the Trial Chamber in the Dokmanovic case, or rather the OTP. Page 655. This is the question by the OTP about Ovcara. "[Previous translation continues] ... [In English] that you saw Sljivancanin in the hospital area. Did you see Sljivancanin again now? "A. Yes. "Q. In this location? "A. Yes. I believe so. I think he passed by us. "Q. Was he alone or with others? "A. No, he was not alone. He was with another two or three officers." [Interpretation] Mr. Zlogledja, well, now, we had the driver yesterday in your OTP statement, several soldiers in the Dokmanovic case, a number of officers. Which is true?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certainly no officers around.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you testified so under oath.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how that was interpreted at the time, but it wasn't the case that he arrived with a number of other officers. He arrived on his own in that military vehicle. He wasn't the one driving. It was his driver, needless to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zlogledja, I must ask you this: You must have been advised by the victims and witnesses protection unit about the importance of an oath?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a transcript here, your words are recorded. In the Dokmanovic case you went on the record as saying that my client was there with two or three or officers, whereas now you claim not to have said this under oath.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that those officers were at Ovcara too. Not just Sljivancanin alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's press on. We shall leave this for future analysis. I am just confronting you with your own testimony from earlier on. Mr. Zlogledja, there are several other things that I need to ask you about. We have heard a great number of witnesses before this Chamber. They also arrived at Ovcara on buses. Victims and witnesses, should I say. Not one of them ever claimed they had seen Sljivancanin at Ovcara, not even when being prompted explicitly by Veselin Sljivancanin's Defence team. I'll ask you a question about that, but probably after the OTP's objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Despite the fact I'm not sure whether this method of putting -- pitching this witness against other witnesses is appropriate, one witness has testified that Sljivancanin was at Ovcara. So it's just -- it's a misstatement in the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I asked the question from the side of the witnesses who were all on buses. All the witnesses who were on those buses, victims, clearly said that they had not seen Sljivancanin there, all these witnesses who were also victims, but fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that's even trickier, Mr. Lukic. Because you are being very particular in framing your question but creating an impression to the witness that that's true of everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precision is precisely what I was after. Nevertheless, I'll try this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is indisputable that different witnesses turned up at Ovcara at different times. Let me ask you this: Mr. Zlogledja, Dodaj Hajdar left the bus with you, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was standing there with you throughout prior to your departure for Negoslavci, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Petar Kuscevic as well, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Standing with you all the time prior to your departure for Negoslavci. Had even arrived before you did outside the hangar, I mean, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see anyone keeping Dodaj Hajdar from watching what was going on?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one stood in anybody else's way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. You spent a great deal of time with him in prison. Did you ever tell Dodaj that you had seen Sljivancanin at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't talk while in prison. We were not there together. We were separated in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which means you never shared this particular observation with him, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And Petar Kuscevic was there with you all the time, right, standing?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was anyone keeping Kuscevic from looking on?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about Dodaj or Kuscevic, do you know of any reason that they may have had to conceal these facts when giving a statement to the OTP or when testifying? Do you know of anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they saw. I don't know what they witnessed. I don't know what they testified. I can only speak for myself. I know what I saw. I know what I witnessed. I know what I said. I can't speak on anyone else's behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Previously I asked you about the time-line in a bid to be a little more specific; 11.00, the barracks, the journey, Ovcara, two hours at the barracks, half an hour before the gauntlet, off the bus, and then another half an hour, roughly speaking, being there. We're looking for a reference point here, for a frame of reference. When did you arrive at Ovcara? Could we say at about 2.00?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was earlier, as far as I could tell. It might sooner have been between 12.00 and 1.00 rather than at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you because you said you arrived at the barracks at about 11.00, you were there for two hours, and it would have taken you about half an hour to reach Ovcara. That's what you said, that's why I'm asking. So it might have been 2.00, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was 2.00. But that's just my take on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you spent half an hour on the bus, and another half hour there when you say my client emerged, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know we heard testimony before this Trial Chamber of witnesses who, at the time, when you claim, and this is testimony on page 2.942 of the 6th of December, and 2.798 of the 2nd of December, of witnesses who at that time saw Sljivancanin at the hospital and even talked with him.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. All I know is what I saw and what I experienced. As for others, I cannot speak on their behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, I read this earlier to you. When your memory was fresher in 1998 in the Dokmanovic case, were you not so exclusive. You said, I believe I saw him, I think he passed by. Why were you using those words then?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall which words I used, but I know beyond dispute that I did see him. I know that he was in charge of the evacuation of the hospital and of the wounded, and I had reasons to pay attention to him the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You knew before the evacuation began, and you had information and that day when you saw him at the hospital, that he was in charge of the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how we -- what we heard, that he was in charge of the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also claim that you had the opportunity to see him on television, at the police station, or I don't know where, before you actually saw him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you described to the Prosecutor how you saw that on television. If I were to tell you that witnesses who were with you at the police station claim that they saw Sljivancanin on television for the first time only when they came back from captivity, what would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about those other witnesses. I know what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when was the last time you watched television at the police station, if you left on the 17th? Can you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We watched for a while, for quite a while. Until the very end, almost.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I claim, and I'm going to, as I say, prove that here, because we do have the video footage of that, that the face of my client and especially his name, his first and last name, was not known to the television viewers before November 20th, actually his name was misstated, his last name, what would you say to that, am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I said the 19th, I'm correcting the transcript, page 83, line 18. I apologise again to the interpreters. This is my problem. I said the 18th of November when we're -- we had the negotiations of the Mitnica group. That is when my client was seen in conversation with representatives of the European Community. Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The footage that we saw earlier here, and that's the footage that the Prosecutor showed you before, this is footage of the 20th of November, and there is no dispute about that. In that footage Sljivancanin is in camouflage uniform and wearing a camouflage cap, exactly the way you described him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After you left, let's say you were released from detention, you did not see him anymore in any newspapers or on any footage?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first time you saw him was when the Prosecution showed you his photographs?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the Prosecution, but when I was speaking with the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The investigator. That was the first time you saw photographs of him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assert, Mr. Zlogledja, that you don't remember faces all that well, because I see from your testimony when you are describing this other officer whom you spoke with briefly at Ovcara and with whom you went to Negoslavci later and with whom you spent more time than the time you spent with my client, first of all you said in the OTP statement that he was a general, later you said that he was a colonel, then you recognised the photograph of General Zivota Panic. Yesterday you did not recognise Zivota Panic on the video footage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time I was not counting and I was not paying attention to ranks. I know that it was a higher rank, but I wasn't really up to noticing the ranks at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zlogledja, I am just telling you what you said, what you stated, and what you looked at. I assume that you said or described what you saw or what you were watching. You said to The Hague Prosecution in a statement that you were shown photographs, you were shown a photograph of a man with the insignia of a general?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you recognised at that time the photograph of General Panic, this was in 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He seemed familiar, but I didn't say 100 per cent that that was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I must say that you were quite specific. Just one second, please. "In the blue file the investigator showed me several photographs. In file number 2 in two photographs there is an officer about whom I believe is the commander whom I described first." So then you indicated that General Zivota Panic, although you just said Panic, but we know on the basis of the photographs that it's General Zivota Panic as the general with whom you talked. And with whom you spent a considerable amount of time, and with whom you said you went to Negoslavci in a vehicle. When you were shown Zivota Panic yesterday, you didn't recognise him. That is why I assert, and you can agree with me, that you do not recognise faces that you saw many years ago, because so much time has passed since then. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the people that I am sure about. If I am not sure about it, I would say I think or it's possible, but I also say I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said in the Dokmanovic case that you think that it was Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I perhaps said that I think, but I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move into private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am going to ask a couple of questions arising from the examination-in-chief today by my learned friend Mr. Smith relating to Negoslavci. In this official note from 1994, about which you say that some parts are not well interpreted, I'm going to read a passage and then you can tell us whether this has been recorded faithfully, your testimony. This is on page 3. The statement by Zlogledja Zlatko indicates that they stayed alive in Negoslavci exclusively because they were guarded by military police of the regular army who were preventing civilians entering the basement from killing them." The same said that they would not permit that because they were in charge of them. All the five days spent in the basement at Negoslavci they were beaten and abused. Is this a faithful reflection of what you said to the inspector in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the truth. It's just that I don't remember saying expressly. But they did protect us at that point in time and they did not allow those -- civilians who were coming in to beat us to take us outside [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now the last question, when you were taken away to Topcider after five days, to Belgrade, did all the people in the basement room leave with you or did some people stay behind?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some -- the four of us went. Some people stayed behind in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I have completed my cross-examination. And I am still unable to turn my microphone off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll get you lessons, Mr. Lukic. Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just a few quick questions in re-examination. I apologise for my lateness earlier. I thought with this new very efficient schedule that we'd be going all day, but -- I thought it was a lunch break, so I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you a couple of questions on a few matters that have been raised during cross-examination. And I suppose the first question I would like to ask you is whether or not on the 20th of November when you are at the Vukovar Hospital, when you're at the barracks, when you were at Ovcara, did you have a watch?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I have a watch? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have any access to clocks that would tell you the exact time that you were at the different places?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you were at the Vukovar barracks, you said that you were very scared as to what was going to happen to you and to others. When you were at Ovcara, how were you feeling at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We felt the same. We were frightened, worried about our lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How did you -- did that affect your ability on how you could tell the time or time periods or not?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it did. In relation to time, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: A question about what was asked of you when you testified in the Dokmanovic case. And it was put to you by one of my learned friends that at the Dokmanovic case you didn't testify in relation to what happened to the men as they were placed in the hangar at Ovcara, nor as to any people being taken out of that hangar, and I would just like to read out your testimony from the Dokmanovic case in 1998. And can you tell me whether or not you agree with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecutor please tell us which of our colleagues asked the question in that way? I don't think that any of the colleagues said that he did not testify in the Dokmanovic case about the hangar. All that was discussed was the police station at Negoslavci. But what my learned friend, Mr. Smith, is asserting was not mentioned at any point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And it wasn't mentioned by Mr. Lukic, but by Mr. Domazet, that this witness didn't give any witness about what occurred inside the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps if I just read the testimony from the Dokmanovic case at page 656, and I would like to put the question to you. "During this period of waiting, were you able to hear what happened to the persons you mentioned being inside the hangar?" And you responded: "Yes, because there was another bus behind us. They all went through that same procedure, so to speak. They would be beaten as they came off the bus and then they would enter the hangars, and in the hangars they were beaten additionally. "As of these beatings did you see these beatings or did you hear the beatings? "Yes, we saw it, and we could also hear the moans and screams." Do you agree that you testified to that in the Dokmanovic case? I just read from your transcript.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And perhaps if we can just go to Ovcara again, you stated in your examination-in-chief that Captain Sljivancanin arrived at Ovcara in a Pinzgauer vehicle with a driver; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: After -- after Captain Sljivancanin got out of that vehicle, do you know what happened to the driver? Do you know whether he stayed in the car or got out with him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when -- and when Captain Sljivancanin approached the men outside -- the soldiers outside of the hangar, was the driver with him? Who else was with him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the driver wasn't there. The driver got out and he was walking around the truck. He got -- or he approached the soldiers and spoke with them by himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And you talked about the time that an investigator from the OTP took a statement from you in 1996, and it was mentioned that you picked out Sljivancanin from photographs that were shown to you. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When the investigator showed you these photographs did, in fact -- were the photographs all of Sljivancanin, or did they include other people as well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, all the other people were around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "other people were around," were there other people in that same photograph, or were other photographs shown to you, in addition to Sljivancanin, of other people?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ZLOGLEDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, other than his, of other people too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And I've finished my questions with you, Mr. Zlogledja.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: But just one brief matter for the record, Your Honour. In relation to a question that was put by Mr. Lukic to the witness, and I think it may have been just a mistake on his part, of course. The witness at page 5532 that was on the bus with this witness, he stated that five or six people descended from the bus, but 10 people were read from the list, and I think that that was the confusion there. But it's in the transcript, just to clarify that. I get a nodding of the head, so I think we are in agreement on that one. Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Smith. Can you tell me, what is the position tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that there is no witness tomorrow on the basis that the testimony this week was going to proceed longer, but on your instructions obviously we have tried to be as brief as we can. And Mr. Grujic unfortunately cannot come until Monday; he's travelling on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. You will be pleased to know that that is the end of the questions in this case. You may now of course leave and go back to your home. The Chamber would thank you for coming here and for the assistance that you have been able to give. We will now adjourn, and we resume on Monday at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of June, 2006, at 12.30 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
